title: Set 258

sentences.ko: 요즘 달걀값 봤어? 어제 열두 개에 7달러쯤 줬어. 애들한테 팬케이크 해 준다고 이미 약속만 안 했어도 안 샀을 거야.
sentences.text: Have you seen what they're charging for eggs now? I paid like seven bucks for a dozen yesterday, and I only got them because I'd already promised the kids pancakes.

alts.text: Eggs are crazy expensive now, right? Seven bucks for a dozen yesterday! I only got 'em 'cause I'd already promised the kids pancakes.
Have you noticed how much eggs cost now? I paid approximately seven dollars for a dozen yesterday, and I only purchased them because I had already promised the children pancakes.

sentences.note: **what they're charging for** 는 그 물건을 얼마에 팔고 있는지를 말할 때 써요. 값이 너무 올랐다고 투덜댈 때 자주 나옵니다. 숫자 앞의 **like** 는 대충 그쯤이라는 뜻이에요.

sentences.ko: 집주인이 계속 살아도 된다고는 하는데 월세가 또 오른대. 그래서 좀 더 외곽 쪽 집을 알아보는 중이야. 근데 돈은 아끼겠지만 사람들을 거의 못 보게 될 거고, 그럴 만한 가치가 있는지 잘 모르겠어.
sentences.text: My landlord says I can stay, but the rent's going up again, so I've been looking at places a little farther out. I mean, I'd save money, but I'd hardly see anybody anymore, and I'm not sure that's worth it.

alts.text: Landlord says I can stay, but rent's going up again, so I'm checking out places a bit farther out. I'd save money, sure, but I'd barely see anyone, and I dunno if that's worth it.

My landlord has said that I may stay, but the rent is increasing again, so I have been considering places a little farther away. I would save money, but I would rarely see anyone, and I am not certain that it is worth it.

sentences.note: **farther out** 은 시내에서 더 떨어진 곳, 외곽을 말해요. **I mean** 은 앞에서 한 말을 이어서 풀어 말할 때 붙여요.

sentences.ko: 커피숍에서 돈 그만 쓰려고 비싼 에스프레소 머신을 하나 샀거든. 근데 쓸 때마다 청소하는 데 15분은 걸려. 그래서 지금은 그냥 세워만 두고 출근길에 여전히 커피를 사 가.
sentences.text: I bought one of those fancy espresso machines because I figured I'd stop spending money at the coffee shop, but it takes like fifteen minutes to clean every time. So now it just sits there, and I still grab coffee on the way to work.

alts.text: Got one of those fancy espresso machines 'cause I figured I'd quit spending money at the coffee shop, but it's like fifteen minutes to clean every time. So it just sits there, and I still grab coffee on my way to work.

I purchased one of those high-end espresso machines because I thought I would stop spending money at the coffee shop, but it takes approximately fifteen minutes to clean each time. As a result, it simply sits there, and I still buy coffee on my way to work.

sentences.note: **I figured** 는 그럴 거라고 생각했다는 뜻이에요. 생각대로 안 된 일을 말할 때 잘 써요. **grab coffee** 는 커피를 간단히 사 간다는 말이에요.

sentences.ko: 허리 때문에 드디어 병원에 갔는데, 의사가 한마디로 괜찮대. 소파에서 일하는 것만 그만두면 된대. 차라리 뭐라도 찾아냈으면 좋았을 텐데, 이제 진짜로 앉는 자세를 바꿔야 하잖아.
sentences.text: So I finally went in about my back, and the doctor basically said I'm fine, I just need to stop working on the couch. I kind of wish she'd found something, because now I actually have to change how I sit.

alts.text: Finally got my back checked out, and the doc basically said I'm fine, I just gotta quit working on the couch. Kinda wish she'd found something, 'cause now I actually have to change how I sit.

I finally saw a doctor about my back, and she essentially told me that I am fine and simply need to stop working on the couch. I almost wish she had found something, because now I actually have to change the way I sit.

sentences.note: **went in about my back** 은 허리 때문에 병원에 진찰받으러 갔다는 뜻이에요. **kind of wish** 는 조금은 그랬으면 좋겠다고 바랄 때 써요.
sentences.situation: 병원 갔다 온 얘기 가볍게 하기

sentences.ko: 솔직히 말하면 알람을 못 듣고 계속 잤어. 잠결에 끈 게 분명해. 눈을 떠 보니 벌써 8시 반이더라고. 그래서 의자에 걸쳐 있던 옷 아무거나 걸치고 뛰어나갔어.
sentences.text: Okay, I'm not going to lie, I slept through my alarm. I must've turned it off without waking up, because when I opened my eyes it was already eight thirty, so I just threw on whatever was on the chair and ran.

alts.text: Totally slept through my alarm. Must've shut it off in my sleep, 'cause I opened my eyes and it was already eight thirty, so I just threw on whatever was on the chair and ran.

To be honest, I slept through my alarm. I must have turned it off without waking, because when I opened my eyes it was already eight thirty, so I simply put on whatever was on the chair and hurried out.

sentences.note: **slept through my alarm** 은 알람이 울렸는데도 못 듣고 계속 잤다는 뜻이에요. **threw on** 은 옷을 대충 급하게 걸쳐 입는 거예요.

reviewed: 1번 한국어: 한국에서 달걀 한 판은 30개라서 a dozen(12개)과 안 맞습니다. 열두 개로 고치고, like seven bucks 에 맞춰 7달러쯤으로 바꿨습니다.
3번 formal: fancy 를 expensive 로 바꾸면 값 얘기로 뜻이 좁아집니다. high-end 로 고쳤습니다.
4번 formal: I somewhat wish 는 원어민이 거의 안 쓰는 말이라 I almost wish 로 고쳤습니다.
5번 casual: 앞부분 Not gonna lie, I slept through my alarm 이 text 와 거의 같아서 첫머리를 바꾸고 뒷부분도 더 말하듯 줄였습니다.
